clue.text: Sticky stuff gives nasty experience in body cavity

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the body-cavity word

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or cavity in the body
a hellish time, a nasty experience, is hell

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note about something sticky and unpleasant found inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin used for varnish, a sticky substance before it hardens.

clue.text: Band's jaunt into the Home Counties

indicators.note: into puts the jaunt inside the Home Counties letters

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a jaunt is a short trip

explanation.surface: A music group's outing into the commuter counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, a band across something.

clue.text: Former copper has left, head seen as free from blame

parts.note: ex- means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A retired policeman quits, and his chief is cleared of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate someone is to clear them of guilt or show they are innocent.

clue.text: Yarn in which car is destroyed in northern city

indicators.note: is destroyed in means the car word is wiped out of the city name

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in the far north of England
the word car as written

explanation.surface: A story about a car wrecked in a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a story, but it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Old-fashioned man on board likely to be wanted

parts.note: cove is dated British slang for a man or chap
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A quaint fellow aboard ship who might be in demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covetable is desirable, the sort of thing people long to own.

clue.text: Cause for regret — I should be no more

definitions.text: Cause for regret — I should be no more

indicators.note: should be says the letter I is to be swapped for the next phrase

parts.note: a pity is a cause for regret
the letter I as written
something no more is over, finished

explanation.surface: A wistful wish that some regrettable thing might vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: In PITY the I gives way to OVER, making P-OVER-TY. Read whole, the clue is a semi-&lit: want is a cause for regret that ought to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and destitution are a cause for regret and something people wish to see abolished.

clue.text: In a cold region that reference work places below Poland

definitions.meaning: describing land near the North or South Pole

definitions.text: that reference work places below Poland
definitions.meaning: a dictionary lists this word straight after the entry for Poland

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry tucked under Poland describing an icy place.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference work is a dictionary, where the alphabetical order puts this word just after Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar means relating to the regions around the Earth's poles, the coldest areas.

clue.text: Even when bad, highly thought of and treated with awe

indicators.note: bad means the word even is scrambled

parts.note: rated means esteemed, highly thought of

explanation.surface: Someone admired and revered even when behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to revere, so a venerated figure is regarded with deep respect.

clue.text: Discharge is strange — the man should be imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means locked inside the strange word

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A prisoner's release seems odd and someone thinks he belongs back in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like release from prison, but it is a bodily secretion. RUM is British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery mucus from the eyes or nose, a bodily discharge.

clue.text: Pest climbing around a plant

indicators.note: around means the turned word goes round the letter a
climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to pest is to pester or worry

explanation.surface: A garden pest climbing round a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns WORRY into YRROW, which wraps round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering herb with feathery leaves, a common wild plant.

clue.text: Heaps of deceptions — get rid of the leader

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is to be removed

parts.note: tricks are deceptions

explanation.surface: A complaint about piles of lies and a call to oust whoever is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricks are stacks of hay or straw, so heaps in a farming sense.

clue.text: True love motivation ultimately for this person working?

definitions.text: True love motivation ultimately for this person working?

indicators.note: working means the letters are set in motion and rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of motivation

explanation.surface: A question about whether love alone drives someone who works unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TRUE LOVE plus N, the last of motivation, are rearranged. The whole clue also describes the answer: someone who works for love, not pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid helper works for the love of the cause, which is the image the whole clue paints.

clue.text: Material two girls put together, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike of the girls' names

parts.note: the names Polly and Esther joined up

explanation.surface: Fabric made by stitching together the efforts of two girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fabric, a kind of cloth or material.

clue.text: See nothing that could help character identification

parts.note: the Holy See is based in Rome
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An optician or detective claiming that seeing nothing could still help identify someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter: in the NATO phonetic alphabet Romeo stands for R, helping identify it over a radio.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio spelling alphabets a codeword is used to identify each letter, and this one names R.

clue.text: Some lethal female? The other one is the wife!

definitions.text: The other one is the wife

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A husband's joke wondering whether a deadly woman is his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband may call his wife his other or better half, the matching partner.

clue.text: Sack comedienne who's a troublemaker?

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
Jo Brand is a British stand-up comic

explanation.surface: A demand to dismiss a comic who stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo Brand is a well-known British comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is an agitator who stirs up unrest, a person who causes trouble.

clue.text: Stormy and sensuous person in past

indicators.note: in places the sensuous person inside the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
a luster is someone who lusts

explanation.surface: A description of a passionate former lover with a tempestuous nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery weather is windy and squally, so stormy.

clue.text: Say more than anyone else, being extreme

parts.note: to utter is to say
most means more than any other

explanation.surface: Being the most talkative in the room shows extremism.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost means furthest or greatest in degree, the most remote or extreme.

clue.text: The man seen among various rectors in cathedral city

indicators.note: seen among puts the man inside the other letters
various means the letters of rectors appear in a different order

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man spotted among a group of clergy in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'rectors' sound like real clergy, but they are only letters; 'various' is the signal to shuffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent has a famous medieval cathedral, so it is a cathedral city.

clue.text: Once again get hold of support back at the front

indicators.note: at the front puts the word for back before the support word

parts.note: the rear is the back
a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab a support again, with the back part at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a suspect a second time is to capture or detain them once more.

clue.text: Former copper leaving pad — a detective

indicators.note: leaving says the word pad departs from the former copper's name

parts.note: Brian Paddick is a former senior Metropolitan Police officer
the word pad as written

explanation.surface: A retired policeman moves out of his flat and becomes a private eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Paddick was a well-known senior London police officer, later a politician; 'pad' looks like his flat but is just letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is old American slang for a detective, as in private dick.

clue.text: Numbers taken in by soldiers offering knowledge

indicators.note: taken in by means the numbers sit inside the soldiers

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers absorbing numbers and so gaining understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is spiritual or mystical insight, a kind of special knowledge.

clue.text: Impassive saint taking cover, hiding love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: An unmoved saint takes shelter while concealing feelings of love.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person shows little emotion, calm and unexcitable.

clue.text: Get hold of former school pupil to be a governor

parts.note: to nab is to seize, get hold of
OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Seizing an old boy of the school to install him as governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was a Mughal provincial governor in India, later any rich and powerful man.

clue.text: Let's not have girl's musical instrument

parts.note: to ban something is to say we won't have it
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A refusal to allow a girl her instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: Section about chaps going to church in paper

indicators.note: about means the section word goes round the others

parts.note: a part is a section

indicators.note: the chaps go to church, so they come after it

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: A newspaper section about men attending church.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin used for writing, and also a kind of stiff paper.

clue.text: Revolutionary distressed almost to the end

indicators.note: almost to the end means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: pained means distressed

explanation.surface: A rebel who stayed upset almost until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' joins 'almost', saying the final letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Paine wrote Common Sense and backed the American and French revolutions.

clue.text: Call Henry up, not an effeminate type

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: to name is to call
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Summoning Henry to prove he is no softie.
explanation.definitionFit: A he-man is a strongly masculine, muscular fellow, the opposite of effeminate.

clue.text: Republic in South American with cruel iron man

indicators.note: cruel treatment knocks the letters out of shape

explanation.surface: A South American keeping company with a harsh, hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruel' looks like a description of the iron man, but it is the signal to rearrange those words.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent state enclosed by Italy, one of the oldest republics.

clue.text: Speck of dust left in lodge

parts.note: a mote is a tiny particle of dust

explanation.surface: A speck of dust has been left behind in a cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel, a lodging place for travellers.

clue.text: Foot of water — consider taking route around

indicators.note: taking a route around means the consider word travels round the water word

parts.note: to see is to consider, as in I'll see
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: A walker thinking about going the long way round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is not a body part or a length here but a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a spondee is a metrical unit of two stressed syllables, one kind of foot.

clue.text: Crusader beat left-winger — Conservative getting in

indicators.note: getting in means the Conservative letter enters between the other pieces

parts.note: to tan is to thrash or beat
a red is a socialist, a left-winger

explanation.definitionFit: Tancred was a Norman leader on the First Crusade, a famous crusading knight.
